classification: Causal final-readiness cost reduction demonstrated; hard 8.33 ms M13 closure fails; no full-suite or shipping gate

method.percentiles: Nearest rank; every sample retained; both strict >8.33 and >11.11 ms counts
method.gpuAlignment: Ordered Composition route/frame correlation, then gpuFrame == geometryFrame == host.frame - 1. GPU scope row is position host.frame - 3, independently asserted to match frame and total in these retained journals.
method.cpuAlignment: Submission is host row at native GPU frame; completion is the following host row. Update contains fenceWait/inspection/hostCallback/validationUpload. Do not sum nested scopes.
method.scopeArithmetic: Preparation is inside cullAndPreparation. Candidate uses existing vertex-input-to-fragment timestamps. Other is total-candidate-cullAndPreparation, not an independent pass. Background/material/scene scopes overlap and must not be summed.
method.publication: Prep publication elapsedMs is existing job-start-to-publication, not complete demand-to-publication; synchronous map/index qualification can precede job start.
method.counts: Only hardware TCS/TES values used as generated draw counts. Counter23-based publication counts may be aliased and are not used as workload or physical validation proof.
method.counterfactual: Removing an entire incoming readiness block is an optimistic arithmetic bound with zero replacement cost, not a measured production correction.
method.losslessJournalLoading: Try sources[mode].jsonPath, otherwise gzip-decompress sources[mode].gzipPath. Verify uncompressedJsonSha256 before parsing. The Markdown contains a standalone Python -B reproduction recipe.

conclusions: Six-frame cause: complete incoming camera-dependent cull/compaction shares the final physical-preparation frame while the existing current owner is rendered. Timed barrier intervals are small compared with dispatches.

Triangle-validation control is slower. Vertex validation demonstrates a bounded causal GPU saving and removes all >11.11 ms observations in this private route; it does not satisfy the updated <=8.33 ms gate.
Final-slice-only savings cannot change the numerous nonfinal >8.33 ms frames; even zero-cost incoming readiness cannot close this responsibility under the new limit.
CPU is not qualified: synchronous diagnostic map construction and first-use index scans remain explicitly accounted for, and were not integrated into the production asynchronous ownership path.
No full-suite, production acceptance, physical-word proof for the new readiness implementation, or shipping gate follows from these timing controls.
